logline: Five women in Monterey, California become entangled in a murder investigation, as the glossy surface of their privileged lives cracks under secrets, trauma, and violence.

renewal.note: Season 3 confirmed in development as of 2025; Francesca Sloane hired as writer and Liane Moriarty working on a follow-up novel due 2026.

bollymeter.basis: 93% on Rotten Tomatoes from 199 critics; a sharp, compulsively watchable murder mystery elevated by Kidman and Witherspoon to something genuinely disturbing about gender, power, and privilege.

pull_quotes.text: Bitingly funny and highly addictive, Big Little Lies is a twisty, thrilling, enlightening ride led by a first-rate cast.
The show's strength is that it makes the experience of inevitable catastrophe so watchable, like a car-crash in slow motion.

seasons.review_body: Premiering in February 2017, Season 1 adapted Liane Moriarty's novel with Jean-Marc Vallee directing all seven episodes. Critics gave it 93% on Rotten Tomatoes from 199 reviews, clustering around two things: the formal elegance of its crime-flashforward structure and the ferocity of Nicole Kidman and Reese Witherspoon's performances. Variety called it like watching a slow-motion car crash you cannot stop watching. The season works as a self-contained drama about domestic violence, class performance, and female solidarity - topics handled with more craft than most prestige cable had managed in years. Audience scores mirrored critical enthusiasm at 95% on the Popcornmeter.

episode_reviews.title: You Get What You Need
episode_reviews.spoiler_free: The finale delivers on the show's sustained tension - the trivia night confrontation is everything the first six episodes have been building toward. Jean-Marc Vallee's direction keeps the climax both lurid and emotionally grounded, and the ensemble cast operates at full force.
episode_reviews.the_moment: The beachfront aftermath as the five women silently align - a tableau critics called the series' defining image.

bollymeter.basis: 85% on RT from 271 critics; Meryl Streep's Mary Louise is the season's legitimate reason to watch, even as critics noted the expanded run felt less precisely controlled than Season 1.

pull_quotes.text: Gorgeous and gripping, Season 2 gives its cast even more juicy drama - especially an excellent Meryl Streep.

seasons.review_body: Season 2 arrived in June 2019 under new creative circumstances - director Andrea Arnold was reportedly sidelined in post-production in favour of showrunner David E. Kelley's cut, a production conflict covered widely in trade press. Critics still returned 85% from 271 reviews, largely on the strength of Meryl Streep's Mary Louise Wright, a character who weaponises politeness as effectively as any villain in prestige TV. The consensus flagged an expanded, somewhat sprawling arc compared to Season 1's tight adaptation. Audience scores were comparable at 84% Popcornmeter. The craft is undeniable; the sense of diminishing returns is also real.
seasons.season_over_season: Trades Season 1's surgical seven-episode precision for a broader canvas; Streep's casting is a genuine upgrade on paper, but production turbulence behind the scenes shows in the pacing.
